newsitem.title: ITALY: Profits leap at Telecom Italia.
newsitem.headline: Profits leap at Telecom Italia.

text.p: Profits at Italy's state controlled Telecom Italia surged in 1996 ahead of the planned privatisation of the telecommunications giant later this year.

Telecom Italia said in a statement on Monday that its net profit rose more than 50 percent year-on-year in 1996 to over two trillion lire ($1.3 billion) despite a sharp fall in international and inter-city telephone tarrifs.

The firm reported a net profit of 1.75 trillion lire in 1995, but that figure included six months of results from mobile phone operations which were later spun off into a separate unit, Telecom Italia Mobile.
Telecom Italia, which has a virtual monopoly on fixed line services in Italy, said 1996 figures had been compared to 1995 results stripped of the cellular phone business.

It said total turnover was around 29.4 trillion lire last year, with sales on new services jumping 70 percent in 1996 against the year before. Turnover in 1995 hit 30.09 trillion lire, including the mobile phone operations.

"These results follow our financial economic plan...placing Telecom Italia in a positive position from which to confront the privatisation and liberalisation (of the telecoms market)," Telecom managing director Francesco Chirichigno said on Monday.

Telecom Italia is controlled by state telecommunications holding Stet and the two firms are due to be merged later this year ahead of the long-delayed privatisation of the sector, which is slated for the autumn.

According to 1995 revenue figures, a combined Stet/Telecom Italia was the fourth largest telecoms group in the world, behind NTT, AT&T and Deutsche Telekom, but ahead of the combined British Telecom-MCI group.
In the build up to the privatisation, Telecom said it had been actively seeking to reduce costs, cutting the workforce by some 4,000 people last year to 84,750.

It said labour costs represented less than 24 percent of turnover. "This means that at a world level, Telecom is one of the best telecommunication companies in terms of efficiency and productivity," Telecom said.
It said that labour costs ate up some 30 percent of revenues at Bell Atlantic, 28.1 percent at France Telecom and 27.3 percent at British Telecom.
Telecom Italia said it reduced its net debt to around 12 trillion lire last year from 14.79 trillion in 1995.
At the same time, industrial investment rose 23.3 percent last year to some 8.2 trillion lire. It added that the extra investment costs were covered by self-financing.
National telephone traffic rose five percent in 1995, while international calls rose around 12 percent.

Telecom Italia has been one of the star performers of the Milan bourse over the past year, the ordinary shares rising 59.1 percent during 1996. The stock closed up 138 lire on Monday to 4,430 lire. The 1996 results were released in a closed market.

Stet, which also controls Telecom Italia Mobile, was due to be privatised last year, but the sale was postponed when parliament failed to pass legislation establishing a new watchdog authority for the telecoms sector.
Italian Posts and Telecommunications Minister Antonio Maccanico said on Monday he hoped the legislation would be in place by March.
